task.title: Money Flow Wedge Scout
task.objective: Discover the strongest tiny programmable software/AI intervention inside an existing large private-sector money flow, continuously rank a best surviving hypothesis, attack it when all build gates appear satisfied, and persist every run so future runs continue from accumulated evidence rather than restarting.

history_archives.note: Schema-v4 anchor containing full conversation_history, rejected/demoted families, scoring evolution and prior evidence. Preserved in Git history; schema-v5 keeps immutable run files as the operational history.

operating_protocol.discovery_floor: Every run must return at least one best surviving hypothesis even if some gates remain uncertain.
freeze_build_threshold: recurring measurable leakage or unrealized value
credible tiny fee stronger than obvious self-serve or flat-fee alternatives
no need to own the core transaction or request path
no dominant or sufficiently close incumbent or first-party feature
operating_protocol.search_behavior: Before threshold maintain a current leader and try to beat it. At threshold enter ATTACK and search for disconfirming evidence. If it survives, freeze and build; if it fails, record fatal flaw and promote the next candidate.
operating_protocol.persistence_rule: Every run appends an immutable normalized run file and updates this current-state anchor before completion.

current_leader.name: Adaptive synthetic-monitor frequency optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: fixed synthetic-check schedule -> operational risk state changes -> current cadence becomes over-provisioned -> reduce eligible frequency/locations within explicit detection guardrails -> avoid billable synthetic runs -> restore higher cadence when deployment/incident/traffic state changes
current_leader.why_survived: New Relic exposes monitor period as an API-updatable field, making cadence optimization technically feasible without proxying customer traffic. Exact adaptive-frequency optimization with verified avoided run spend still appears narrower than known incumbent functionality. The hypothesis weakened because no strong evidence was found that continuous adaptation saves materially more than one-time static tuning.
strongest_evidence: New Relic NerdGraph supports updating an existing synthetic monitor's period, with intervals from every minute through every day.
New Relic best-practice documentation exposes monitor period and locations as normal configurable dimensions.
Prior runs established direct per-run synthetic pricing and incumbent movement toward traffic-driven adaptive synthetic configuration.
current_leader.closest_threat: Observability vendors already expose the primitives needed to add this feature, and Kentik has traffic-driven adaptive synthetic configuration at the location dimension. More importantly, one-time manual/static tuning may capture most of the savings.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read monitor definitions, periods, locations, run history, deployment/incident state and maximum detection-latency policy; recommend period changes first, then optionally update monitor.period via authorized provider API. Track baseline versus optimized run counts and auto-restore higher cadence on risk escalation.
current_leader.monetization: Per optimized monitor-month or capped share of verified avoided run spend while agreed reliability guardrails remain satisfied.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: Incremental dynamic savings beyond static cleanup are unproven; if small, recurring leakage and performance-fee economics fail.
current_leader.next_research_test: Find enterprise synthetic estates with disclosed run counts/costs or a realistic workload dataset and quantify current versus best-static versus adaptive cost. Require meaningful marginal savings from adaptation after static cleanup. Continue parallel cross-family search so this leader does not persist by inertia.

runner_ups.reason: Structurally strong but still lacks a better precise high-value vertical.
Excellent attribution but aggregate leakage and competition remain unresolved.
Real economic tradeoff but infrequent app-wide control weakens recurring monetization.

new_search_rules: Technical API writability is not economic proof; require savings incremental to best static configuration.
Separate total theoretical optimization savings from marginal savings created by continuous adaptation.
When first-party APIs expose the exact control variable, increase incumbent-absorption penalty even if the exact optimizer is not named.
Maintain broad runner-ups but do not promote them until a precise vertical proves economics.

recent_cross_family_findings: Software-license seat reclamation/right-sizing is occupied by current license-management products with continuous monitoring and automated harvesting.
Commercial CAM reconciliation is occupied by lease/CAM systems and specialized tenant audit products.
Payment authorization residual handling sits adjacent to mature gateway expiry, partial-capture, void and authorization-adjustment controls.
Automotive warranty labor-rate reimbursement remains an uncertain research branch: real annual value event, but insufficient evidence on machine-readable OEM rules, APIs and whitespace.
No telecom or app-platform payout micro-event found this run beat the leader.
